longFormInfo: Ferdowsi's verse epic of the Persian kings from the creation of the world to the Arab conquest of the seventh century.

authorshipNote: Ferdowsi drew on an earlier prose Shahnameh compiled in 957 and on verses by the poet Daqiqi, which he incorporated.

sources: Djalal Khaleghi-Motlagh, 'Ferdowsi, Abu'l-Qāsem i. Life', Encyclopaedia Iranica
longFormInfo: Written over about thirty years; a first version was finished in 994 and the final version in 1010, dedicated to Mahmud of Ghazni.

surviving: In hundreds of manuscripts. The oldest dated one, of 1217, in the Biblioteca Nazionale Centrale, Florence, holds only about half the poem; the oldest complete copy, of 1276–77, is in the British Library. The most celebrated copies are illustrated manuscripts such as the Great Mongol Shahnameh and the Shahnameh of Shah Tahmasp.
significance: At about 50,000 couplets, it is the national epic of Iran and the Persian-speaking world, written in a Persian with few Arabic loanwords.
legacy: It preserved Iran's pre-Islamic legends and history, shaped modern Persian, and has been recited and illustrated for a thousand years; heroes such as Rostam remain household names.
shortSummary: Ferdowsi's Persian epic poem of about 50,000 couplets, completed in 1010, telling the history of Iran's kings from mythical times to the fall of the Sasanian Empire.
longSummary: It runs from the mythical first kings through the heroic age of Rostam to the historical Sasanian dynasty and the Arab conquest.
Ferdowsi wrote it in the Samanid and early Ghaznavid period, when Persian was re-emerging as a literary language.
Its manuscripts became the principal vehicle of Persian miniature painting.

It has been recited by professional storytellers (naqqals) in coffee houses and zurkhanehs for centuries, recited on Yalda night and taught in schools, and translated into many languages; Mohl's French edition (1838–1878), Arthur and Edmond Warner's English verse translation (1905–1925) and Dick Davis's prose-and-verse translation brought it to Western readers.
